newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan teachers refuse to end strike.
newsitem.headline: Angolan teachers refuse to end strike.

text.p: Angolan teachers will not end their five-week-old strike until the government pays their back wages, the leader of the teachers' union said on Tuesday.
"The strike will continue," Miguel Filho, general secretary of the 23,000-strong National Teachers Union, told reporters.
"We don't have any intention of calling this off until the government pays our back wages," Filho said, adding Angolan teachers were owed wages for the first four months of the year.
Most civil servants in Angola went on strike this month but all except the teachers returned to work after a week when they received assurances from the government that back wages would be paid.

Angolan economists say the government is trying to avoid paying the approximately 130,000 civil servants all at once, fearing that an injection of such a large amount of money into Angola's weak economy might set off inflation.
